# OpenSCAD files

`shape.import_scad { source, file?, name?, material?, process?, definition? }` (or `./ise import part.scad`, or the person drops the file on the view) makes a live shape: its program runs the file through Iṣẹ́ Studio's OpenSCAD reader with the file's top-level number values as the shape's parameters (`width = 40; // [20:100]` becomes parameter `width` from 20 to 100, the comment above it its label), so it scrubs, links and configures like any shape. The reader covers the language (modules and functions with defaults, recursion, children(), the last-assignment-wins scoping, $fn/$fa/$fs passed down, if/for/intersection_for/let, list comprehensions, function literals, vectors and matrices, echo, assert) and geometry (cube, sphere, cylinder, polyhedron, square, circle, polygon with holes, translate, rotate including axis-angle, scale, resize, mirror, multmatrix, color, offset, hull, minkowski, union, difference, intersection, linear_extrude with twist and scale, rotate_extrude). Cubes, cylinders, spheres and extrusions stay exact in STEP; `$fn` from 3 to 16 makes true polygons (a hex nut trap stays six-sided), otherwise curves are round to Iṣẹ́ Studio's tolerance; coloured top-level pieces become parts with the colour as their material's look. `text()` uses Iṣẹ́ Studio's lettering (Inter); `include`/`use` of other files, `import()`, `surface()` and `projection()` are refused with the reason (paste a library's modules into the file). In your own programs: `openscad(source, { width: p.width })`.

Export: `/export/<id>.scad` gives an imported file back with the parameters' current values appended (OpenSCAD's last assignment wins); any other shape exports as a polyhedron per part (its mesh at the export tolerance).

The prelude also has `solid.minkowski(other)` (a solid swept over every point of another — rounded offsets of any shape; faceted in STEP) and `solid.transform([[a, b, c, tx], [d, e, f, ty], [g, h, i, tz]])` (any affine map; exact unless it shears).
